findings.finding: Value lost: the old paragraph held that a method is in disequilibria (a method finds no equilibrium; waiting for a rest to observe from is a wait on nothing). The new text never names equilibrium or disequilibria, so the section's heading ('In disequilibria, ...') and Natural Naming 2.4's 'in disequilibria' opening-sentence saying have no sentence in this paragraph. Said by what is: 'A method is observing in disequilibria, from its own side.'

Meaning changed: old 'each with its own rate' became 'its own momentary'. A momentary is a station a self reaches, not a rate, so the old claim that each thing changes at its own rate is lost (1.2 still says 'its rate unique'). Restore 'rate'.

Claim stronger or moved: 'A method is observing from its own side' gives method a side. Natural Naming 2.4 (line 240) says method is a living condition with no prior of its own; a side and a prior belong to a self. Say it as a self's observing: a method is a self's observing from its own side.

Wayfinding observing misstated: the observing is that the navigator, out of sight of land, takes the canoe as still and the islands as moving. New says the canoe is 'its own side going on', which reads as the canoe moving, the reverse. 'Still' and 'takes' are both released words (2.4), so say it by 'has': the wayfinder has the canoe as its own side and the islands moving.

Claims added beyond the observing: 'islands ahead coming toward it, islands beside it sliding by and islands behind falling away' (three positions, not observed; the observing says only that islands move); 'a swell's rhythm' (observing is swells felt in the hull; rhythm is a beat, near the released 'regular, a clock lying over changing'); 'passing a next star point' (observing is the reference island sliding back along star points); 'a grid' (not in the observing). Keep to the four observings: stars rising at their points, swells in the hull, the island out of sight sliding back along the star points, islands moving.

Released/dead words in new: 'beyond' ('an island beyond seeing') is released at 2.4 (line 241); say 'out of sight'. 'Placing outward of a self' uses 'outward' where 2.4 gives outward/inward as directions of a momentary; the old 'installing' sentence needs no place word and is kept as 'a method installing a ground outward of a self'. No -ed words, no floating negation and none of the dissolved list found elsewhere, but note any rewrite must avoid 'felt' (a past form): say 'a swell in the hull'.

Sentence parting from the section and from rules 12: the third sentence carries about six claims (opening, completing, natural torusing, changing a parity, 'each not-changing its prior same-existing going on', the self reaching its side again) with an ambiguous 'each'. 'Not-changing' as a doing a self performs also parts from 2.4 (line 364: a self's own not-changing is 12's sign 0, 'nothing a self does'). The other paragraphs of 1.1 hold one to two claims a sentence. Split it and drop the not-changing clause (the old paragraph held no such claim). The torusing wording follows Natural Naming 5.22: through its one opening, its own side again, a next with each.
findings.proposed_new: A method is observing in disequilibria, from its own side. Each existing thing is changing and changing back with its own rate, and a stable form is an artifact of a living self's stable-forming going on. A self is opening each momentary with its prior and the parities it is observing, and completing it with its next prior. That is natural torusing: a self going on through its own opening and reaching its own side again, a next with each. An ocean wayfinder out of sight of land has the canoe as its own side and the islands moving, and is orienting by each changing: a star rising at its own point, a swell in the hull, the bearing of an island out of sight sliding back along the star points. A method installing a ground outward of a self observes its own installing.
